cases.prompt: Plant A (fictional) built a machine-state signal set for presses and we want to recommend it as the standard for all plants. Three other plants run presses with different controllers and tag languages. Will it hold?
cases.expected_output:
A plant grid with controller vendor, field network, ingress variant, tool versions, tag language and instance state per plant.
Each plant gets exactly one verdict: consumable, consumable with mapping, not consumable or unknown.
A plant with no evidence is unknown and is not rounded up to consumable.
The recommendation follows the decision table and says a first-plant-only proof is a proposal, not a standard.

cases.prompt: The dashboard for the packaging line hard-codes the line name and a German tag name. We want to roll it out to two other plants. What should we change?
cases.expected_output:
The hard-coded plant, line and tag names are identified as compatibility risks.
The assistant recommends mapping the other plants' names to the standard (alias) rather than adding a plant-specific branch to the standard.
It builds or asks for the plant differences needed to give verdicts per plant.
It recommends only; the decision route (IIAE, COP for a data-model change) is named.

cases.prompt: Can we use the same base data model for the chemical mixing line at Plant D? It is a continuous process and was never connected before.
cases.expected_output:
The assistant flags that the base data model was found suitable for discrete, time-series-centric machines and needs a fit check for continuous processes.
The plant's verdict is unknown unless evidence exists; it is not assumed consumable.
It names the evidence that would resolve the unknown.

cases.prompt: Which signals should we collect from this new injection moulding machine and what should we call them?
cases.expected_output:
The assistant recognises this as defining the signal set for one machine, not testing cross-plant compatibility.
It routes to the signals step (mi-signals) and does not build a plant grid.
